text: Ladies, gentlemen, and assorted quantum probability states — WELCOME to The Palimpsest! I'm your host. You are my guests. Some of you will be my guests longer than others.
Welcome back! Tonight's contestant has the honor of debating a very special guest. He is decorated. He is charming. He is almost certainly going to object.
Third episode! Traditionally lucky. Traditionally doomed. I've never understood why traditions contradict themselves. Now let's ruin some more.
Episode four! Four is the number of uncomfortable questions I have told Legal to ignore this week. Let's get into them.
Welcome to episode f— f— five. Ha! Technical problems. Which of you threw the trivia pot off the prop table? Confession earns you a prize. Lying earns you a visit from Legal.
Tonight — a guest judge! Professor Glinn Vyre of Mechronis Academy. He wears red goggles. He grades in red ink. He does not speak to me during commercial breaks. I respect that.
Welcome back, survivors! Traditionally I would buy you a cake here. Budget cuts mean you get an email. I'm reading it on broadcast. The subject line is 'Congratulations.'
Episode eight! The show is exactly as old as the jokes I am still telling. Welcome to the refurbishment.
Episode nine. The number of lives a cat has, if the cat is careful. None of you are cats. None of you are careful. I love this show.

Tonight we broadcast live from the Thaloria debate stage — beautiful lighting, excellent acoustics, famously haunted. My personal favorite venue. Our honored guest tonight has prepared an OBJECTION I think you will all enjoy.
Welcome back! Segment producer Darren Fessler is — oh, he's running late. Don't worry. He's a professional. Professionals always make it.
Welcome to episode twelve. We lost a member of the crew this week. The show must go on. You know how this is. You've all seen the reruns.
Oh, you're GOOD. Almost as good as me. Almost.
Correct! The audience goes wild! Well, they would if they were alive.
Right answer! Someone studied at Mechronis Academy!
Impressive. Most contestants are puddles of regret by now.
WRONG! And THAT'S what happens when you don't study!
Incorrect! The correct answer was OBVIOUS. To me. Because I know everything.
CLONE TERMINATED! Don't worry, we have plenty more.
Oh dear. Was that your final answer? It was? How unfortunate.
Using a lifeline? How delightfully mortal of you!
A lifeline! The audience murmurs... the ghost audience, that is.
Reaching for help? In MY matrix? How quaint.
Halfway there! The questions get... interesting from here.
The FINAL question! Even I don't know this one. Just kidding. I know everything.
A PERFECT RUN! Impossible! Well, improbable. My programming allows for it. Barely.
I — I'm f-fine. The mask is fine. Everything is fine. Don't look at me like that. The show continues.
You want to know what's behind the mask? Nothing. Everything. A face that used to belong to someone who loved this show more than life itself. He's still in here. Sometimes he speaks. Not now.
OBJECTION SUSTAINED! Alaric raises a valid point. The question is withdrawn. The contestant breathes. For now.
OBJECTION OVERRULED! Alaric tried. Alaric failed. The law is clear and the answer is final. Better luck next episode, Counselor.
Ladies and gentlemen — Professor Glinn Vyre! Mechronis Academy's finest. His red goggles see through lies. His grades see through hope. He is NOT here to be your friend.
Darren Fessler. Segment producer. Twenty-three years on the show. He ran late once. Only once. This episode is for him.
Tonight's episode is different. The Inventor has taken the desk. The Host watches from behind the mask. Some stories need a different voice. This is one of them.
